vicrental

Purpose

vicrental helps renters in Victoria explore rental prices by suburb. It includes a cleaned dataset, functions to summarise and rank rents, and a Shiny app that answers: how have rents changed, which suburbs are the most or least expensive, and where can I afford to live?

Data

The rentals dataset contains median weekly rents and the number of new lettings for flats and houses across Victorian suburbs, by quarter and number of bedrooms.

  • Source: Victorian Department of Families, Fairness and Housing (DFFH) Rental Report, compiled at https://publicdata.au/d/vic-rents-by-suburb/.
  • Preparation: data-raw/rentals.R reads the raw CSV, removes aggregate rows (“All properties”, “Group Total”) and rows with missing values, splits the property description into number of bedrooms and property type, and derives year and quarter.
  • Columns: see ?rentals.

Installation

You can install the development version of vicrental from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-thunchanok19")

Launch the app 

library(vicrental)
run_app()

The app opens on an About tab and has four tabs in total:

  • About: explains who the app is for, the question it answers, how to use the controls and what the fields mean. Each other tab has a “How to read this” note under its output.
  • Compare suburbs: compare median rents across up to three suburbs over time.
  • Top 10 rankings: rank the highest or lowest rent suburbs in a selected quarter and year.
  • Affordability: find suburbs within a weekly rent budget for a selected property type and number of bedrooms.

Functions

  • summarise_rent(): median rent over time for chosen suburbs.
  • top10_rent(): the highest or lowest rent suburbs in a selected quarter and year.
  • affordable_suburbs(): suburbs within a weekly rent budget.
  • run_app(): launches the Shiny app.

Documentation: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-thunchanok19/

AI Appendix

I used AI as a coding and writing assistant while building this package, app and site. The topic, dataset, research question and design decisions were mine, and I tested, edited and checked all AI-assisted code myself.

  • Package structure: explained how the files in an R package fit together (DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R/, data-raw/, inst/, roxygen comments) and how to set them up with usethis and devtools.
  • Data preparation: suggested approaches for cleaning the raw CSV in data-raw/rentals.R, such as splitting the property description into bedrooms and property type, and removing aggregate rows.
  • Shiny app: helped write and debug code for the app, including the tabbed layout, interactive plotly charts, the reactable table, colours and theme, and the empty-state messages.
  • Package functions: helped draft and debug the exported functions and their roxygen documentation.
  • Documentation: gave feedback on grammar and wording, and suggested what to include in the README, the app’s About tab and captions, and the vignette.
  • Troubleshooting: helped diagnose errors, including a GitHub token (401) error when installing the package from GitHub and a pkgdown setup error.
